key_terms.الْهِيمِ: Thirst-stricken camel, specifically one suffering from intense thirst and disease.

ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of 'shurb al-haym' mean in Surah Al-Infitar?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'al-haym' refers to camels suffering from intense thirst after a long journey, highlighting the disbelievers' desperate, unquenchable consumption of the boiling water of Hawiyah. This imagery underscores the futility of their punishment, as they drink greedily yet remain unsatisfied, mirroring their spiritual emptiness in worldly life. The comparison serves as a vivid metaphor for the transient nature of their relief before the eternal torment resumes.
